epics.summary: Production TDD-split: tech-lead writes tests, weak local model implements

stories.summary: Add _resolve_test_author_backend with a hard same-model refusal guard
stories.description: First phase of TDD_SPLIT_PRODUCTION_PLAN.md. Adds role-scoped backend/model resolution for a new 'test_author' role, mirroring the existing _resolve_planner_backend pattern (pipeline_mcp_server.py ~L1034) used by GUIDED_DECOMPOSITION_PLAN.md's planner step. Unlike the planner (which defaults to mirroring dispatch's own backend/model when unconfigured), the test-author role must default to OFF (return (None, None)) when unconfigured, and must explicitly refuse to return a backend/model pair that resolves to the SAME concrete backend+model as the story's own dispatch backend/model. This guard exists because tests/benchmark/tdd_split_experiment.py's isolated 3-way experiment on ratelimiter_inspect proved same-model test-authorship (gpt-oss writing its own tests, then gpt-oss implementing against them) is actively HARMFUL: the implementer read-loop-parked in 24s without ever writing the impl file, versus a stronger different-model test-author (glm) producing 31 valid portable tests and a clean implementer pass. This story is purely the resolution/guard logic - no dispatch-phase wiring yet (that's TDDSPLIT-2).
stories.agent_instructions:
Read pipeline_mcp_server.py's existing _resolve_planner_backend function (around line 1034) in full first - this new function must mirror its exact shape and priority order (plan_role_config -> env var -> model_registry.json's roles map -> fallback), changing only the fallback behavior and adding the same-model refusal. Also read role_registry.py's resolve_role and load_registry functions in full to understand RoleResolution's shape and how an unconfigured role is distinguished from a configured one - no schema changes are needed to model_registry.json or role_registry.py; role names are plain dict keys, nothing hardcodes a fixed role list (confirmed: grep for VALID_ROLES/KNOWN_ROLES in both files returns nothing).

Write a failing test FIRST (TDD), in a new test file test_test_author_backend.py (or add to an existing pipeline_mcp_server test file if there's a clear precedent - your call, but do not modify any existing test without explicit approval per CLAUDE.md Step 4).

Implement _resolve_test_author_backend(dispatch_backend: str, local_model: str, plan_role_config: dict | None = None) -> tuple[str | None, str | None] in pipeline_mcp_server.py, placed near _resolve_planner_backend for discoverability. Contract:
1. Resolve a provider_override the same way _resolve_planner_backend does: plan_role_config.get('test_author', {}).get('provider') OR os.environ.get('PIPELINE_BACKEND_TEST_AUTHOR') OR role_registry.load_registry().get('roles', {}).get('test_author', {}).get('provider').
2. If no provider_override is found (role entirely unconfigured), return (None, None) - this is the secure/neutral default (Core Principles: ship disabled by default) given variant A's proven harm. Do NOT fall back to mirroring dispatch_backend/local_model the way the planner does - that fallback would silently reproduce the harmful same-model variant A for any operator who enables PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT without also configuring a distinct test-author role.
3. If a provider_override IS found, call role_registry.resolve_role('test_author', plan_role_config=plan_role_config, registry=registry, model_fallback=lambda: None) and get back a RoleResolution.
4. CRITICAL SAFETY CHECK: after resolution, compare the RESOLVED (provider, model) pair against (dispatch_backend, local_model). If they are equal (same backend AND same model), return (None, None) instead of the resolved pair, and log a clear warning (e.g. via print or the module's existing logging pattern - check how _run_planner or nearby functions log warnings) stating that the test_author role resolved to the same backend/model as dispatch and was refused. This comparison must be on the RESOLVED values, not the config source, so it also catches an operator setting PIPELINE_BACKEND_TEST_AUTHOR to a different env var that happens to point at an identical concrete model/endpoint.
5. Otherwise return the resolved (provider, model) pair.

Tests must cover (positive AND negative per CLAUDE.md testing standards):
- Unconfigured role (no plan_role_config entry, no env var, no registry entry) -> returns (None, None).
- Configured via plan_role_config resolving to a genuinely different backend/model than dispatch -> returns that (provider, model) pair.
- Configured via PIPELINE_BACKEND_TEST_AUTHOR env var -> same as above, confirms env var priority matches _resolve_planner_backend's pattern.
- Configured via model_registry.json roles.test_author entry -> same, confirms registry fallback works.
- SAME-MODEL REFUSAL (the critical regression test): plan_role_config or env var resolves test_author to the IDENTICAL (backend, model) pair as the dispatch_backend/local_model arguments -> returns (None, None), not the resolved pair. Test this for at least two distinct ways of arriving at the same resolved value (e.g. explicit plan_role_config match, and env-var match) to prove the check compares resolved values, not config source.
- Priority order: when both plan_role_config and the env var are set to different (non-dispatch-matching) values, plan_role_config wins (mirrors _resolve_planner_backend's own priority - verify by reading its implementation, don't assume).
- role_registry.resolve_role raising RoleRegistryError (a malformed registry entry) should NOT be silently swallowed here if _resolve_planner_backend doesn't swallow it either - check the existing function's error-handling behavior and match it exactly (this function must have the identical failure contract as its sibling, not a stricter or looser one).

Confirm each new test fails for the right reason before implementing (e.g. ImportError/AttributeError for the not-yet-existing function, NOT a same-model pair incorrectly passing through). Testable success criteria: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test_test_author_backend.py` (or wherever you place the tests) passes; full suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` has zero regressions (currently 1139 tests, per the 2026-07-18 session baseline - if your count differs, note why in your summary).

stories.summary: Wire a test-author dispatch phase into dispatch_story, gated by PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT=off|on, fail-open to monolithic dispatch
stories.description: Second phase of TDD_SPLIT_PRODUCTION_PLAN.md. Adds the actual pre-executor dispatch phase to pipeline_mcp_server.py's dispatch_story, using TDDSPLIT-1-ROLE-RESOLUTION's _resolve_test_author_backend to decide whether to run it. Unlike GUIDED_DECOMPOSITION_PLAN.md's planner step (a single bounded complete() call), this phase is a FULL agent-loop dispatch via backend.get_backend('dispatch', name=...).dispatch(...) - the same primitive the main executor uses - because writing a good test suite requires running pytest and iterating, not a single completion. This is the single most safety-critical story in the plan: a broken/timed-out/crashed test-author dispatch must NEVER leave a story blocked or silently degrade to 'no tests at all' - it must fall back to today's exact existing monolithic behavior.
stories.agent_instructions:
Read pipeline_mcp_server.py's dispatch_story function in full (around line 3015-3200), paying particular attention to: (a) the existing worktree-setup block (around line 3040-3066, creates the branch/worktree, or reuses one for a resuming story), (b) the existing PIPELINE_DECOMPOSE planner-checklist step (around line 3156-3190) as your closest structural precedent for how a pre-executor phase is gated, invoked, and fails open, and (c) how backend.get_backend('dispatch', name=...).dispatch(...) is called for the main executor (find the call site further down in the same function) - your new test-author dispatch call must use the identical Backend Protocol contract (same dispatch() signature: prompt, system, model, allowed_tools, cwd, log_path, append), just with a test-authoring prompt and cwd pointed at the story's worktree.

Also read backend.py's OllamaDriver.dispatch (~line 952) and ClaudeCliDriver.dispatch (~line 273) to understand the AgentHandle(pid=...) return contract and how the caller must poll/block for exit - tests/benchmark/tdd_split_experiment.py's dispatch() helper function (in this repo, written 2026-07-18) demonstrates exactly this poll-and-reap pattern (os.waitpid with WNOHANG in a timeout loop) and can be used as a direct reference for the blocking logic, though production code should live in pipeline_mcp_server.py, not import from tests/benchmark/.

Write failing tests FIRST (TDD). Do not modify any existing test in pipeline_mcp_server's test suite without explicit approval (CLAUDE.md Step 4) - add new tests to a new file or an existing file with a clear precedent for dispatch_story tests, your call.

Implement the new phase, inserted in dispatch_story AFTER worktree setup and BEFORE the existing PIPELINE_DECOMPOSE planner-checklist step (both flags must be independently usable - a story can have PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT on, PIPELINE_DECOMPOSE on, both, or neither, with no interaction assumed yet - that composition question is explicitly out of scope for this story, deferred per the plan's section 5 open questions):

1. Read PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT env var (default 'off'). If not 'on', skip the whole phase - existing behavior completely unchanged (this must be verified by a byte-for-byte regression test that PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT=off, or unset, produces an IDENTICAL dispatch_story code path to before this story - mirror how GUIDED_DECOMPOSITION_PLAN.md's own PIPELINE_DECOMPOSE=off regression test was written, search the codebase for it as a model).
2. If 'on', call _resolve_test_author_backend(...) (from TDDSPLIT-1). If it returns (None, None) - either unconfigured or the same-model refusal fired - log this clearly and skip the phase (proceed to existing behavior unchanged). This is NOT an error path, it's the designed-safe default.
3. Check story-level eligibility (a new story field, e.g. story.get('tdd_split') truthy - the exact field name and validation is this story's call, but must be explicit opt-in, not inferred from agent_instructions prose; document whatever name you choose clearly in a comment and in this story's PR description). If the story hasn't opted in, skip the phase.
4. Idempotency check: if the worktree already shows evidence a test-author phase already ran (e.g. a git log marker, a sentinel file, or some other detectable signal - your design call, but it must survive a rework redispatch reusing the same worktree, matching how GUIDED_DECOMPOSITION_PLAN.md's planner step checks for an existing .agent_plan.md before re-planning), skip re-running the test-author dispatch. Reworks act on the SAME tests; they must not get a fresh test-authoring pass.
5. If all the above allow it: build a test-authoring prompt from story['agent_instructions'] plus a fixed suffix (write ONLY the test file for the story's target functionality, do NOT create the implementation file, confirm the tests fail with an import/red state via pytest, cover negative and boundary cases per CLAUDE.md's testing standard) - this generalizes tests/benchmark/tdd_split_experiment.py's phase1_prompt() from that experiment's hardcoded ratelimiter_inspect SPEC_RULES to the story's own agent_instructions, since production stories vary per task.
6. Dispatch via backend.get_backend('dispatch', name=test_author_backend).dispatch(prompt, system=..., model=test_author_model, allowed_tools=..., cwd=worktree, log_path=..., append=False) and block until exit using the poll-and-reap pattern referenced above, with a bounded timeout (reuse whatever timeout config dispatch_story's own executor dispatch already uses, do not invent a new config knob unless the existing one is unsuitable - check first).
7. FAIL-OPEN CONTRACT (the most safety-critical property here): on ANY failure - non-zero exit, timeout, exception, or the dispatch producing no new commit in the worktree - log the failure clearly and proceed to dispatch the MAIN EXECUTOR exactly as dispatch_story does TODAY when PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT is off: i.e. with the story's ORIGINAL, unmodified agent_instructions (no pre-seeded tests, no augmented prompt). This must be an explicit, directly-tested code path, not an assumption. On success, proceed to the executor dispatch as TDDSPLIT-4 will define (that story adds the 'don't touch the tests' prompt augmentation - this story's executor-dispatch call can be left calling the EXISTING unmodified prompt-building logic for now, since TDDSPLIT-4 is a separate PR; just ensure the executor dispatch happens after a successful test-author phase without you having to guess at prompt augmentation here).

Tests must cover (positive AND negative per CLAUDE.md testing standards), likely via mocking backend.get_backend to avoid real subprocess dispatch in unit tests (check how existing dispatch_story tests mock the backend layer and follow that exact pattern):
- PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT unset/off -> byte-for-byte identical behavior to before this story (regression guard).
- PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT=on but _resolve_test_author_backend returns (None, None) -> phase skipped, existing behavior unchanged, no test-author dispatch call made.
- PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT=on, backend resolves to a genuinely different backend/model, story opted in, no existing worktree marker -> test-author dispatch IS called with the expected prompt/cwd/model.
- Story did NOT opt in (tdd_split field absent/false) -> phase skipped even with PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT=on and a valid resolved backend.
- Existing worktree marker present (simulating a rework redispatch) -> test-author dispatch phase is skipped, no re-dispatch.
- Test-author dispatch times out / returns non-zero exit / produces no new commit -> falls back to calling the main executor dispatch with the ORIGINAL agent_instructions, unmodified - assert the exact prompt content passed to the executor dispatch call in this fallback case to prove it's unaugmented.
- Test-author dispatch succeeds (mocked non-zero... mocked SUCCESS with a new commit) -> main executor dispatch is still called afterward (this story doesn't need to verify the SUCCESS prompt augmentation, just that dispatch proceeds).

Confirm each new test fails for the right reason before implementing. Testable success criteria: the new test file/tests pass; full suite has zero regressions (baseline 1139 tests + TDDSPLIT-1's additions, verify current count with a full pytest run before you start and report the delta in your summary).
dependencies: Add _resolve_test_author_backend with a hard same-model refusal guard

stories.summary: Add and validate an explicit story-level opt-in field for the TDD-split phase
stories.description: Third phase of TDD_SPLIT_PRODUCTION_PLAN.md. TDDSPLIT-2-DISPATCH-PHASE's implementer chose a story-level field name/shape for opt-in eligibility (e.g. story['tdd_split']) as an inline design call within that story. This story formalizes it: ensures ingest_plan validates the field's type/shape at ingest time (fail loud on a malformed value, per this repo's existing pattern of validating story['backend'] at ingest - see pipeline_mcp_server.py around line 2818-2825 for the precedent), documents it in the README's plan-schema section alongside the other story fields (persona/model/risk/backend), and confirms the field defaults to falsy/absent-safe (a story with no tdd_split field must behave completely unchanged, matching today's behavior with PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT=on but no opted-in stories).
stories.agent_instructions:
First, read TDDSPLIT-2-DISPATCH-PHASE's merged implementation (find its PR/commit - check git log for the story key or a matching commit message) to see the EXACT field name and shape that story's implementer chose. Do not assume a name - read the actual code. This story's job is to harden that choice, not redesign it, unless you find it's unworkably ambiguous (e.g. accepts any truthy value with no validation) - if so, note the change clearly in your PR description as a deviation from TDDSPLIT-2's inline choice, with justification.

Read pipeline_mcp_server.py's ingest_plan function and its existing story['backend'] validation (around line 2818-2825, 'Valid story["backend"] values at ingest time' around line 2773) as the precedent to mirror: validate the new eligibility field's type (e.g. must be a bool, or an explicit enum if TDDSPLIT-2 used something richer) at ingest time, and raise a clear, actionable error (not a bare KeyError) on an invalid value - matching this repo's existing fail-loud-at-ingest philosophy for other story-level fields.

Write failing tests FIRST (TDD), added to ingest_plan's existing test file (find it - do not modify existing tests, only add new ones per CLAUDE.md Step 4):
- A story with the field set to a valid value ingests successfully and the manifest preserves it.
- A story with the field absent ingests successfully (existing behavior, unchanged) and the manifest reflects 'not opted in.'
- A story with the field set to an invalid type/value raises a clear validation error at ingest time (not silently coerced, not a bare exception from deep inside the code).
- A full-plan ingest (multiple stories, some opted in, some not) round-trips correctly through the manifest.

Also update README.md's plan-schema documentation section (search for where 'backend'/'persona'/'model'/'risk' story fields are documented - likely near the ingest_plan/save_plan tool descriptions) to add this new field with a one-line description and its default (falsy/absent = today's unchanged behavior, no test-author dispatch phase runs regardless of PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT).

Confirm each new test fails for the right reason before implementing. Testable success criteria: the new ingest_plan tests pass; full suite has zero regressions; README's plan-schema section accurately reflects the new field per CLAUDE.md's Definition of Done ('documentation is updated if the change alters externally visible behavior').
dependencies: Wire a test-author dispatch phase into dispatch_story, gated by PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT=off|on, fail-open to monolithic dispatch

stories.summary: Augment the executor prompt with 'never touch the tests' steering after a successful test-author phase
stories.description: Fourth phase of TDD_SPLIT_PRODUCTION_PLAN.md. When the test-author dispatch phase (TDDSPLIT-2) succeeds and produces pre-seeded tests, the main executor's prompt must be augmented with an explicit 'do not modify the test files' steering directive - otherwise the implementer may 'fix' a test it disagrees with, defeating the whole mechanism. This exact steering line already exists, proven, in pipeline_mcp_server.py's _REWORK_PLANNER_SYSTEM constant ('NEVER edit, rename, weaken, or delete the test files (anything matching test_*.py) to make a test pass - if a test fails, the bug is in the implementation, so fix it there.') - this story reuses it verbatim, it does not design new prompt language.
stories.agent_instructions:
Read pipeline_mcp_server.py's _REWORK_PLANNER_SYSTEM constant in full (search for 'NEVER edit, rename, weaken, or delete the test files') to find the exact proven steering language to reuse verbatim. Read TDDSPLIT-2-DISPATCH-PHASE's merged implementation to find exactly where in dispatch_story the main executor's prompt is built, and where that story left a marker/return value indicating whether the test-author phase ran successfully this dispatch.

Write failing tests FIRST (TDD), added to whichever test file TDDSPLIT-2 used (do not modify its existing tests, only add new ones).

Implement: when the test-author phase (TDDSPLIT-2) completed successfully this dispatch (i.e. pre-seeded tests exist in the worktree from that phase, not from a rework's inherited state), append the reused steering line (verbatim, or lightly adapted only if a grammatical connector is needed to splice it into the executor's existing prompt-building code - do not paraphrase or weaken the wording) to the executor's prompt before dispatch. When the test-author phase did NOT run this dispatch (off, skipped, or failed-and-fell-back per TDDSPLIT-2's fail-open contract), the executor's prompt must be byte-for-byte identical to today's existing prompt - no steering line, no changes at all.

Tests must cover:
- Test-author phase succeeded this dispatch -> executor prompt contains the exact reused steering line.
- Test-author phase off/skipped/failed-and-fell-back -> executor prompt is IDENTICAL to the pre-TDDSPLIT-2 baseline (byte-for-byte regression guard - this is the critical negative test, since TDDSPLIT-2's fail-open contract explicitly promises an unmodified prompt in the fallback case, and this story must not accidentally break that promise by adding steering language unconditionally).
- A rework redispatch reusing an existing worktree with a test-author commit from a PRIOR dispatch (not this one) - confirm your logic correctly distinguishes 'test-author phase ran THIS dispatch' from 'a test-author commit exists in the worktree from before' (these are different conditions; TDDSPLIT-2's idempotency check already skips re-running the phase on a rework, but this story must still decide whether the steering line applies on that rework's executor redispatch too - the correct answer is YES, the steering should apply on rework redispatches too since the tests are still off-limits, so make sure your marker/condition captures 'pre-seeded tests exist from a test-author phase, whether this dispatch or a prior one on this worktree' rather than only 'this exact dispatch call ran the phase').

Confirm each new test fails for the right reason before implementing. Testable success criteria: new tests pass; full suite has zero regressions; a manual read of the final executor prompt in both the augmented and unaugmented cases confirms the steering line is reused verbatim from _REWORK_PLANNER_SYSTEM, not reworded.
dependencies: Wire a test-author dispatch phase into dispatch_story, gated by PIPELINE_TDD_SPLIT=off|on, fail-open to monolithic dispatch
